title: v2.15 adds the quicid.elbv2.k8s.aws pod mutating webhook with failurePolicy Fail — a custom webhookNamespaceSelectors value puts it on every readiness-gate namespace

detection.reason: the webhook does not exist before the upgrade, and the chart value webhookNamespaceSelectors is not a projected fact; the hint names the installed LBC pod webhook and the command prints its namespaceSelector — a selector that is not the default pod-readiness-gate-inject label is a custom one and will be copied onto the new Fail webhook

remediation: By default the new webhook only matches namespaces labelled elbv2.k8s.aws/quic-server-id-inject=enabled, so nothing changes. If the chart is installed with a custom webhookNamespaceSelectors value, that selector replaces the QUIC default and the Fail-policy pod webhook lands on every namespace it selects (typically the readiness-gate ones): pod creation there blocks whenever the controller is down. Set the value back to the default or add podMutatorWebhookConfig-style scoping before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfigurations,validatingwebhookconfigurations -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .webhooks[] | select(.name | test("k8s\\.aws$")) | "\(.name) failurePolicy=\(.failurePolicy) namespaceSelector=\(.namespaceSelector // {} | tojson)"'  # the LBC admission webhooks installed on this cluster and the failure policy each runs with
